rationale: C24 is the clear drafting parent. The child expressly distinguishes itself from the March 23, 1948 directive, then reuses that directive's unusually specific description of the same coal operators, union, wage agreement, industry, and interstate-commerce predicate. It also reproduces the same Board-of-Inquiry machinery and operative sequence almost verbatim, changing chiefly the status of the threatened work stoppage and the reporting deadline. C01 and C15 use the same statutory form, but neither matches the child's parties and factual setting as closely as C24.

shared_material.child_excerpt: there exists a labor dispute, other than that referred to in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 23, 1948 ... between coal operators and associations signatory to the national Bituminous Coal Wage Agreement of 1947 and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America
shared_material.parent_excerpt: there exists a labor dispute between coal operators and associations signatory to the National Bituminous Coal Wage Agreement of 1947 and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America
shared_material.explanation: The child explicitly references C24's date and repeats its distinctive identification of the same parties and agreement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry ... engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce ... will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: such dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce ... will imperil the national health and safety
shared_material.explanation: The same detailed statutory and industry predicate is adapted from an existing strike to a threatened strike or lockout.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before June 23, 1948. Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence ... until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 5, 1948. Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence ... until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.explanation: The operative provisions are virtually identical in language and sequence, with only the reporting deadline changed.
